central_finding.title: the frozen wetting convention is the negation of the cited source's, so the closure realises the complementary contact angle
central_finding.source_definition: R1 (Phys. Rev. E 95, 033306, p.9): nw = grad(g) with g the fluid-solid binary matrix, i.e. fluid -> solid

central_finding.implemented_invariant: angle(F, n_w) = theta_c is imposed; measured on the final fields as 64.9/94.2/122.0 deg for prescribed 60/90/120 (case-04) and 62.7/118.6 deg (case-07)

confirmations.method: exact synthetic spherical cap fed to contact_angle_circle_fit
confirmations.result: a true 60 deg cap returns 120.0; the instrument returns 180 - theta at every tested angle (30/60/90/120/150)
fitted circle R=6.68 zc=4.95 with wall at z=1; psi = +0.997 at (cx,cy,z=zc) so the centre of curvature is inside the red phase; cos(theta_liquid) = -(zc-z_wall)/R gives 125.96 deg

confirmations.method: raw droplet field, all three arms

confirmations.result: interface x(y) is 0.669 lu smaller at the wall than at the centre for prescribed 60 and 0.708 lu larger for prescribed 120; Pc = -1.023x and -1.081x of 2 sigma cos(theta)/h, i.e. sign inverted with the correct magnitude
the prescribed-60 wetting capillary expels the liquid (psi in the capillary goes +1 -> -1), reservoir rises 13 -> 14, red mass exactly conserved at 4480.0

central_finding.instrument_defect: contact_angle_circle_fit computes cos(theta) = (zc - z_wall)/R; for a drop on the +z side of the wall the correct relation is cos(theta_liquid) = -(zc - z_wall)/R. The docstring, the case-04 README, metrics.json.phase_convention and the pass-04 header all label the returned value as 'theta measured through psi>0 liquid/red'.
